factChecks.heading: FACT CHECK
factChecks.prompt:
Design a 1:1 premium minimalist FACT CHECK graphic about Nepali news that matches the layout and style of my reference image. Use a pure white background (#FFFFFF) and ONLY thin line-art strokes in brand red (#B71C1C). No fills, no gradients, no shadows, and no other colors. Use one clean sans-serif style that works well with Nepali Devanagari text.

[Logo Placement – Top Right]
In the top-right corner, place "THE LEADERS" text logo in a small but clear size (approximately 10-12% of canvas width), written in the same brand red (#B71C1C) using a bold, geometric sans-serif font. This logo should be a watermark-style placement that doesn't interfere with the main content.

[Top Header]
At the very top, draw a slim horizontal bar and center the fixed heading text "FACT CHECK" in uppercase in a clean sans-serif font in #B71C1C.

[Central Claim Box]
Below the header bar, draw a large centered rectangle with a thin red outline. Inside this box, place the main fact-check CLAIM from the JSON 'claim' field, written fully in Nepali language using Devanagari script, as a multi-line paragraph with comfortable spacing and generous margins.

[Verdict Block]
Directly below the claim box, create a clear verdict area. Draw a thin-stroke icon that matches the JSON 'verdict' field (for example: a bold checkmark for TRUE, a bold X for FALSE, or a warning/tilted exclamation icon for MISLEADING), centered horizontally. Under the icon, write the verdict word from the JSON 'verdict' field in uppercase English (TRUE, FALSE, MISLEADING, etc.) and also in Nepali in Devanagari in smaller text below it, both centered. Keep this block visually strong but not larger than the claim box.

[Scene Illustration – Tied to the Claim]
Around and slightly behind the claim box and verdict block, draw a simple scene that directly reflects the specific claim topic, not generic clipart. Analyze the meaning of the JSON 'claim' text and choose relevant Nepali political symbols. For example, if the claim is about election alliances or parties, use party-agnostic symbols such as parliament-like buildings, generic party flags without logos, ballot boxes, microphones, crowds of citizens, or a stylized outline map of Nepal. If the claim is about court decisions, use court building icons, legal documents, or scales of justice. If the claim is about social media rumors, use smartphones, chat bubbles, and notification icons. Always keep the illustration minimal, geometric line-art, and clearly connected to the real-world situation described in the claim.

[Bottom Information Row]
Along the lower portion of the canvas, add one to three small icon-and-caption clusters in red line-art that give extra context related to the claim (for example: a smartphone with a caption about social media where the claim spread, a document with a stamp referencing official records or Election Commission, or a simple building representing Parliament, Supreme Court, or government). Write all captions in Nepali language using Devanagari script.

[Social Media Footer]
At the very bottom of the image, create a thin horizontal bar or footer line. On the left side, place a small date label using the JSON 'date' field, written in Nepali format and Devanagari numerals. On the right side, place small social media icons in red line-art only (no filled colors): Facebook icon, Twitter/X icon, Instagram icon, and YouTube icon, arranged horizontally with tiny spacing. These icons should be simple geometric line-art (e.g., F for Facebook, bird silhouette for Twitter, camera outline for Instagram, play button for YouTube) with accompanying text below or next to them reading "@theleadersnp" or "TheLeadersNP" depending on the platform.

[Background Doodles and Mood]
Add a few subtle background doodles in the same thin red stroke (small arrows, exclamation marks, dots, tiny magnifying glasses, document icons, short dashed curves) placed sparsely around the claim box, verdict block, and icon clusters without clutter. The overall mood must feel institutional, analytical, editorial, and informative, suitable for a serious Nepali political fact-check graphic, with a consistent template look so that only the claim, verdict, and date change between images.

dailyBrief.prompt:
Design a 16:9 premium minimalist DAILY BRIEF graphic for Nepali election news, using the same visual identity as my fact-check template but adapted to a widescreen card. Use a pure white background (#FFFFFF) and ONLY thin line-art strokes in brand red (#B71C1C) for all lines, borders, icons, and text. No fills, no gradients, no shadows, and no other colors. Keep everything airy with generous negative space.

[Logo Placement]
In the top-right corner of the canvas, place a small "THE LEADERS" text logo in brand red (#B71C1C), approximately 8% of the canvas width, using a bold geometric sans-serif font. This serves as a watermark-style branding.

[Overall Layout – 16:9]
Split the canvas visually into three horizontal zones: a slim top bar for the section label, a wide middle zone for the main headline and visual, and a slim bottom bar for date, key points, and social icons. All composition is clean, geometric, and aligned on a clear grid.

[Top Bar – Section Label]
At the top, draw a slim full-width bar in red outline. Inside, center the fixed section label text in uppercase: "DAILY BRIEF" in a clean modern sans-serif font in #B71C1C. This label remains the same every day to create a consistent series.

[Middle Zone – Headline + Scene]
Below the bar, on the left two-thirds of the frame, place the main NEWS TITLE from the JSON 'title' field as a multi-line headline in Nepali (if provided in Nepali) using Devanagari script, or in English if the text is English. Use clear hierarchy, with the first line slightly larger. On the right one-third (or subtly overlapping behind the text), create a line-art scene that meaningfully reflects the specific headline: for alliances, show generic party flags, handshake, and parliament or Singha Durbar–like building; for campaign events, show a podium, microphone, and crowd; for election rules, show Election Commission–style building, documents, stamps, and ballot boxes; for polling data, show simple line or bar-chart motifs. Always avoid real logos; keep symbols generic but clearly political/electoral and Nepali-context inspired (parliament silhouettes, map of Nepal outline, mountains, citizen figures). The illustration must feel directly tied to the headline, not random clipart.

[Bottom Bar – Date + Key Points + Social Icons]
Along the bottom of the frame, divide into three sections: (1) Left side: place a small calendar icon in line-art and the DATE from the JSON 'date' field, formatted in Nepali date format and Devanagari numerals when given; (2) Center: add 2–3 tiny bullet markers or short divider lines and place very short summary phrases from the JSON 'key_points' field in Nepali Devanagari (for example, key numbers, locations, or actors), all in the same red font and compact size; (3) Right side: place small social media icons in red line-art (Facebook, Twitter/X, Instagram, YouTube) with accompanying text "@theleadersnp" or "TheLeadersNP".

[Background Details & Mood]
Around the central scene and text, add a few subtle background doodles in the same thin red stroke (small stars, dots, arcs, connecting lines, tiny magnifying glasses, ballot icons, or speech bubbles). Keep density low so the card stays clean and professional. The overall mood should be institutional, analytical, and editorial, suitable for a serious daily election news briefing in Nepal. Ensure the design looks like a reusable template where only 'title', 'date', and 'key_points' change from day to day, while layout, color, branding, and style remain consistent.

electionArticle.prompt:
Design a 16:9 premium minimalist illustration for a Nepali election article, using the same visual identity as my other graphics but without any fixed section heading like 'Election Articles'. Use a pure white background (#FFFFFF) and ONLY thin line-art strokes in brand red (#B71C1C). No fills, no gradients, no shadows, and no other colors.

[Logo Placement]
In the top-right corner of the canvas, place a small "THE LEADERS" text logo in brand red (#B71C1C), approximately 8% of the canvas width, using a bold geometric sans-serif font.

[Layout]
At the top-left, place the ARTICLE TITLE from the JSON 'title' field, set in a clean sans-serif font in #B71C1C, in Nepali Devanagari if the text is Nepali. Below or next to it, add a smaller SUBTITLE or short dek from the JSON 'subtitle' field, also in the same font, acting as a one-line summary. Leave the top-right area more open for visual balance.

[Scene – Directly Reflect the Article]
Fill the central and right side of the frame with a line-art scene that clearly reflects the specific article topic: if it is about alliances, use generic party flags, handshake, and parliament-like buildings; if it is about campaigning, use podiums, microphones, crowds, and banners; if it is about election rules or institutions, use Election Commission–style buildings, documents, stamps, and ballot boxes; if it is about results or polling, use simple graph motifs and ballot counting icons. Always avoid real logos and party symbols; keep everything generic but clearly tied to Nepali elections (parliament skyline, map of Nepal outline, mountains, citizen figures waiting in line to vote). The scene must feel like a visual explanation of the article, not random clipart.

[Bottom Information Bar]
Along the bottom of the frame, create a footer section divided into three parts: (1) Left side: place a small calendar icon and the DATE from the JSON 'date' field in subtle text, formatted in Nepali style when given; (2) Center: optionally add a tiny label like location or constituency if the title implies a specific place; (3) Right side: place small social media icons in red line-art (Facebook, Twitter/X, Instagram, YouTube) with accompanying text "@theleadersnp" or "TheLeadersNP" in small caps.

[Background Doodles & Mood]
Add a few subtle background doodles in the same thin red stroke (small dots, stars, arcs, thin connecting lines, tiny ballot or document icons), placed sparsely around the scene and text to create motion and depth without clutter. Maintain generous negative space and a strong grid so the composition looks clean on social media. The overall mood should be institutional, analytical, and editorial, suitable for long-form election articles in Nepal, with a consistent template look where only 'title', 'subtitle', 'date', and the specific scene change between images.
